common.machineNote: These open in Google's translation proxy. We publish two languages we can actually proofread, and we say so rather than shipping nine we cannot.
home.heroBody: Every one of them carries a serial number, a revision, an expression set and a licensable performance range. Manufactured, not lucky.
home.rosterNote: Everyone here has a number and a revision. The revision is not decoration — it counts how many times this character was torn up and rebuilt. Where there is no delivered plate, we say so.
home.methodNote: This is not 'generate a picture with AI'. It is a production line with rework, reversals and a cull.
home.pipeline.0.title: Casting brief
home.pipeline.0.body: Decide how this person thinks before deciding what they look like. Build it the other way round and the character dies by the third film.
home.pipeline.1.title: White model
home.pipeline.1.body: Build, proportion and range of motion are locked on the white model first. Get this layer wrong and every later revision is rework.
home.pipeline.2.title: Surface
home.pipeline.2.body: Face, hair, wardrobe, expression set. Multi-reference locks one person down — across ten films he has to be the same face.
home.pipeline.3.title: Performance
home.pipeline.3.body: Put them in a scene. The ones who hold stay on the roster; the ones who do not go back in. The revision number is how many times that happened.
home.kitNote: An actor becomes worth something by being used. So we hand you the same character seed we use ourselves — paste it into any model and you get this person, not a lookalike. Free, no permission needed.
home.pactNote: Five things we are willing to say in public about who gets paid. Written down so you can hold us to them.
home.stanceBody: Every actor here is animated. CG, drawn, obviously not a person — you can tell in a second, and you are supposed to. Not because photoreal is out of reach. Because we are not going there, and we are not letting anyone take our characters there either.
home.worksNote: The first films are still being made. No invented numbers, no invented clients, no invented view counts — one goes live, one goes up.
home.castingBody: License a roster actor, commission your own, or co-produce. Three doors, all open. Bring a film, a brand, or just an idea.
roster.metaDescription: The full SWIMMER PARTY roster of original AI actors — codes, revisions, specifications and casting status.
roster.intro: The code is the identity, the revision is the résumé. {castable} castable now, {building} still on the line — we do not call an unfinished one finished.
roster.buildingNote: Character locked, white-model stage. They move to castable the day the plate is delivered.
actor.noPlateBody: This actor is still at the white-model stage. The plate, expression set and wardrobe replace this frame on delivery.
actor.seedEnNote: The seed is written in English on purpose: image models follow English far more reliably than Chinese, whoever you are. Paste it as it is.
works.metaDescription: The SWIMMER PARTY slate: original comedy shorts and series in production.
works.intro: This house opened in {year}. Nothing on this slate is invented — one goes live, one goes up; what is in progress says it is in progress.
works.outro: Want one of our actors in your film?
kit.metaDescription: Free character kits for SWIMMER PARTY's AI actors — the character seed, register notes and reference sheets, handed over so anyone can remix them.
kit.intro: A synthetic actor gets valuable the same way a human one does — by being used. So the kit is open. Paste the seed into any image model and you get this person, not a lookalike.
kit.manifestNote: Status is literal. AVAILABLE means it is on this site right now and you can test it in thirty seconds. Everything else says what it actually is.
kit.seedsNote: Only actors whose look is locked have a seed. An actor still on the white model has no face to describe, so that row says so instead of shipping a guess.
kit.seedPending: No seed yet — still on the white model
kit.rulesNote: Short enough to actually read. Two things you may do freely, three things you must not.
pact.metaDescription: SWIMMER PARTY's public position on who gets paid when a synthetic actor makes money — a draft, published so it can be held to.
pact.intro: Two things, written down where you can hold us to them: what we refuse to build, and how the money gets split when there finally is some. Both were easier to say now, before anyone is arguing about a number.
pact.draftNote: This is a published position, not an executed contract. The settled lines are settled. The percentages are marked open on purpose — we will not print a number we have not honoured yet.
pact.partOneNote: The first half of this page is a refusal. It comes first because it is the one that costs us money.
pact.partTwoNote: The second half is a promise. Work should feed the people who did it. If a character breaks out, that money should not land in one account.
pact.termsTitle: What is settled, what is not
pact.outro: Made something with one of our actors? Send it. That is the whole process.
studio.metaDescription: How SWIMMER PARTY builds an AI actor: the full line from brief to white model to plate to performance.
studio.intro: SWIMMER PARTY is the synthetic talent house of PieAI Studio. We do not take outsourced rendering. We build our own actors and then we lend them out.
studio.beliefsNote: These four decide what everyone on the roster looks like, how they talk, and when they get cut.
studio.beliefs.0.title: A face is not a character
studio.beliefs.0.body: Plenty of people can generate a good-looking face. Very few can make the same face still be the same person, saying the same kind of thing, in the tenth film. The difference is not the model. It is whether a specification was written down and held to.
studio.beliefs.1.title: Version numbers are honest
studio.beliefs.1.body: We print how many times a character was torn up right on the roster. VERSION 6 OF 10 means the first five were not good enough. Hiding that is what looks guilty.
studio.beliefs.2.title: The white model comes first
studio.beliefs.2.body: Proportion, build and range of motion get locked before anyone talks about skin or clothes. Reverse the order and the character is just a poster that moves.
studio.beliefs.3.title: Comedy is the hardest test
studio.beliefs.3.body: Whether a character holds up is decided in comedy. Tragedy can be papered over with music. If it is not funny, it is not funny.
studio.stackNote: This site and every actor on the roster run on PieAI's own toolchain, not on something bolted together.
studio.stack.0.name: Swimmer UI Kit
studio.stack.0.note: One source for buttons, panels and tokens
studio.stack.1.name: React Three Fiber
studio.stack.2.name: Next.js
studio.stack.2.note: So the roster can actually be found
studio.stack.3.name: PGS
studio.outroBody: We take commissions too — an actor built for your brand or your film and nobody else's.
casting.metaDescription: License a SWIMMER PARTY AI actor for your film, or commission an original one built only for you.
casting.intro: Three routes. Bring nothing but an idea and we will tell you which one you are on.
casting.routes.0.title: License a roster actor
casting.routes.0.body: Use someone already on the roster. Character, expression set and performance range exist today — this is the fast route.
casting.routes.1.title: Commission an actor
casting.routes.1.body: We build a new one for you down the whole line: brief, white model, plate, performance sign-off. Delivered with the full specification sheet.
casting.routes.2.title: Co-produce
casting.routes.2.body: We bring the actors and the production, you bring the subject, the channel or the money. The film belongs to both of us; the character stays on the roster and keeps working.
casting.contactBody: Tell us: what kind of project, roughly when, and which actor you want (or what kind of actor you want). One sentence is fine — we will ask the rest.
casting.availableNote: The ones in development can be discussed too — whoever asks first gets first call on delivery.
casting.remixNote: Not a brand, just want to make something? The kit is free and you do not need this page.
notFound.body: This one is not on the roster. Maybe we have not built them yet.
assets.intro: Every image of {name} is a separate full-size original with no text on it. Pick what you need and download one at a time, or sign in to take the whole set.
assets.note.turnaround: Front, three-quarter, side and back. Full body, transparent background.
assets.note.face: Close-ups that lock the face. The most important references you can give a model.
assets.note.expression: Twelve core emotions, plus speaking and eyes closed.
assets.note.wardrobe: Same person, another outfit, four angles.
assets.note.detail: Hands, the back of the head, signature props.
assets.legacyNote: An older black-background image, to be replaced by the new set.
assets.none: This actor's assets are still being made.
assets.noSeed: The look is not locked yet, so there is no seed.
assets.guestCooldown: Guests can download one full-size image every {seconds} seconds. {remaining} seconds to go.
assets.guestHint: Sign in with Swimmer to select several, download a pack or build a sheet.
assets.signInTitle: Take the whole set with a Swimmer account
assets.signInBody: It's free. The same account also works in:
assets.format.zipNote: One transparent PNG per image, with the profile and terms of use.
assets.format.sheetNote: For tools that take a single reference image.
assets.format.modelNote: Picks and combines images to fit the model's reference limit, with an English note.
assets.overLimit: {count} selected. This model takes {limit}, so the {limit} most important will be kept.
assets.failed: That could not be completed. Please try again.
